generator.note: Compressed payload bytes depend on the zstd version and level. Uncompressed structures (HEAD, AUTH, LTBL, LAYR's version field, LHAS, REE streams, directory, trailer) are exact. Sealed units are exact too: every nonce, salt and key is derived from a fixed SHAKE-256 seed, so regeneration is deterministic. Those values are public test data; real encoders must draw them from a CSPRNG.

invalid.description: LTBL's entry_count says seven while the table holds six entries, so the table does not end where the header says it does.
invalid.name: ltbl-entry-count

invalid.description: The last entry claims one further entry for its layer, so the sum of 1 + additional_sector_count over the layers' first entries runs one past the table the header declares.
invalid.name: ltbl-entry-count-overrun

invalid.description: Layer 0 carries sectors 0, 1 and 2, and its last two entries are written in the order 0, 2, 1: the ids descend where the table requires them to ascend.
invalid.name: ltbl-sector-ids-descending

invalid.description: Layer 0's two entries both name sector 0, so the layer carries one sector twice instead of two sectors once.
invalid.name: ltbl-sector-id-duplicate

invalid.description: Layer 1's only entry names sector 3. Sector 0 is primary and implicitly present on every layer with data, so a layer's first entry is sector 0's.
invalid.name: ltbl-first-entry-not-sector-zero

invalid.description: Entry 0 names directory index 2, which is the LTBL chunk itself, so the slice has no frame to be read out of.
invalid.name: ltbl-first-layr-not-layr

invalid.description: Entry 1 claims 0x00FFFFFF bytes even though it is the last slice of the frame it names, so its end lies past the frame's decompressed output.
invalid.name: ltbl-offset-past-frame

invalid.description: Entries 2 and 3 are two slices of one frame and both now start at offset 0, so layers 2 and 3 would be read out of the same bytes.
invalid.name: ltbl-slices-overlap

invalid.description: Layer 2's entry names no LROV chunk although the file carries one for that point: first_lrov is 0 exactly when a (layer, sector) has no overrides. Because an LROV payload carries no identity, that chunk is now unreachable - this file violates lrov.orphan as well, and the check order decides which is reported.
invalid.name: ltbl-first-lrov-zero

invalid.description: Entry 0 names directory index 2, which is the LTBL chunk, as the override set of its point, so the entry points at a chunk that carries no overrides.
invalid.name: ltbl-first-lrov-not-lrov

invalid.description: Entry 0 names the same LROV chunk as layer 2's entry, so one override set is claimed by two points at once. The payload carries no layer and no sector, so a reader cannot tell which of the two it belongs to - it would have to apply layer 2's override to layer 0 as well, or ignore one of them.
invalid.name: lrov-shared-chunk

invalid.description: The file carries an LROV chunk that no entry names. An LROV payload carries no layer and no sector - the entry that names the chunk is what places it - so these overrides can never be applied to anything, and a reader that silently ignores them prints the wrong timings.
invalid.name: lrov-orphan-chunk

invalid.description: An LROV payload is truncated JSON, so the override set cannot be read at all.
invalid.name: lrov-not-json

invalid.description: An LROV payload carries wait_time_before_cure_ms = 500.5. A wait time is a whole number of milliseconds, so a fractional value is not a duration this format can express.
invalid.name: lrov-wait-fractional

invalid.description: Layer 0 stores all-black as tag 0x00 with run_count 0 instead of the empty-layer form.
invalid.name: run-count-zero-all-black

invalid.description: A LAYR container declares version 2, which no reader implements; the frame behind it is well formed, so only the version refuses the file.
invalid.name: layr-container-version

invalid.description: The LAYR frames are compressed without their content size. A writer MUST declare it (spec 4.10), because the descriptor's size_uncompressed is the container's length and the reader has nothing else to size the frame's output from.
invalid.name: layr-content-size-absent

invalid.description: The first LAYR frame's header declares one byte more than the frame decompresses to, so its output cannot be allocated or checked against the declaration.
invalid.name: layr-frame-size-lie

invalid.description: The first block header of the first LAYR frame is rewritten to the reserved block type 3, so the frame cannot be decompressed.
invalid.name: layr-frame-corrupt

invalid.description: ZDIC.dict_id is rewritten while the frames keep the id of the dictionary they were compressed with, so every LAYR frame disagrees with the file's dictionary.
invalid.name: layr-dict-id-mismatch

invalid.description: The frames are compressed with a trained dictionary but the file carries no ZDIC chunk, so their dictionary ids name a dictionary no reader can find.
invalid.name: layr-dict-id-without-zdic

invalid.description: Every sealed LAYR frame is bound to unit index 0 instead of the directory index of the chunk that carries it. Each frame is intact, but a reader that authenticates it under the chunk's own index must refuse the file - which is what stops a ciphertext from being swapped between two LAYR chunks, since with one unit per chunk an all-zero index would authenticate in either place.
invalid.name: crypt-unit-index-binding

invalid.description: Layer 1's entry claims one further entry, so the walk takes layer 1 and layer 2 for one layer and reaches layer 2 of a four-layer file; the entries no longer cover every layer the header declares. The merged layer also holds sector 0 twice, which is what the entries it swallowed carry.
invalid.name: ltbl-layer-index-range

invalid.description: The file's only LAYR frame declares a decompressed size of 2147483647 bytes, some four thousand times what the slices pointing into it could hold, so a reader that sizes its buffer from the declaration allocates two gigabytes for a layer group of a 64 by 48 display.
invalid.name: layr-allocation-bound

invalid.description: The file carries a ZDIC chunk while every LAYR frame declares no dictionary (dictionary id 0), so the dictionary is present but nothing in the file refers to it.
invalid.name: presence-zdic-unused

invalid.description: META.sectors has two entries with sector_id 1, so the sector's timing is defined twice over.
invalid.name: meta-sectors-shape

invalid.description: META.sectors[0].material_index is 3 while META.materials holds one entry, so the sector names a material that is not there.
invalid.name: meta-sector-material-index

invalid.description: One byte of merkle_root is flipped, so recomputation from layer_hashes disagrees.
invalid.name: merkle-root-mismatch

invalid.description: Layer 0's stored leaf hash is altered and merkle_root recomputed to match, so only hashing the actual bytes catches it.
invalid.name: layer-hash-mismatch

invalid.description: The file's layers carry two sectors but the header does not set MULTI_SECTOR, so a reader that trusts the flag prints one sector per layer and never notices the rest.
invalid.name: multi-sector-flag-clear

invalid.description: No layer of the file carries more than one sector, but the header sets MULTI_SECTOR, so the flag promises a structure the file does not have.
invalid.name: multi-sector-flag-set

invalid.description: The trailer CRC-32C does not match the file bytes.
invalid.name: trailer-crc-mismatch

invalid.description: META carries normal_exposure_ms = 2500.5. Durations are exact whole milliseconds, so a fractional value is not a duration this format can express.
invalid.name: meta-exposure-fractional

invalid.description: The file header sets ENCRYPTED but there is no AUTH chunk, so no session key can ever be derived.
invalid.name: encrypted-flag-without-auth

invalid.description: AUTH.cipher_id is XXXX, which names no algorithm.
invalid.name: auth-cipher-unknown

invalid.description: AUTH.mode is 0: neither a password nor a machine binding is declared, so the session key is unreachable.
invalid.name: crypt-mode-empty

invalid.description: The password section declares Argon2id iterations = 99, above the recommended ceiling of 10; it is otherwise coherent, so only the cost rule refuses it.
invalid.name: crypt-argon2-budget

invalid.description: AUTH declares a 64-byte password section, one byte short of the fixed section size.
invalid.name: crypt-password-len-short

invalid.description: AUTH.mode sets machine-binding but the machine section is empty: no recipient can ever unwrap the session key.
invalid.name: crypt-machine-len-empty

invalid.description: ZDIC's descriptor does not set the encrypted flag although the file is encrypted; its bytes are sealed regardless, so the flag is the only disagreement.
invalid.name: crypt-plaintext-content

invalid.description: One ciphertext byte of the first sealed LAYR frame is flipped, so its AEAD tag must fail; a reader must not decompress or parse a frame it cannot authenticate.
invalid.name: crypt-tag-corrupt

invalid.description: PROF.profile_type is "resin", which is not one of the three defined types.
invalid.name: prof-type-unknown

invalid.description: PROF.profile_name is an empty string.
invalid.name: prof-identity-empty

invalid.description: PROF settings carry a zero normal exposure.
invalid.name: prof-settings-exposure

invalid.description: PROF settings carry a zero layer height.
invalid.name: prof-settings-layer-height

invalid.description: PROF cure curve has dp_um = 0.0, which no resin can have.
invalid.name: prof-cure-curve

invalid.description: PROF.profile_uuid is not a UUID.
invalid.name: prof-uuid-malformed

invalid.description: PROF.materials is an empty array, which the META.materials shape rules forbid.
invalid.name: prof-materials-shape

invalid.description: A PREV chunk sets reserved flag bit 5 alongside role 1; only bits 0-3 carry the role.
invalid.name: prev-flags

invalid.description: A PREV payload does not begin with the PNG signature. A loose reader ignores previews and must still accept the file; a strict validator rejects it.
invalid.name: prev-not-png

invalid.description: The embedded scene is a JSON array rather than a VOXL document: the payload begins with neither the V2 magic nor the V1 document marker. A loose reader never looks inside the chunk and must still accept the file; a strict validator rejects it.
invalid.name: voxl-not-voxl

invalid.description: An extension sets the critical bit, so a reader that does not implement it must refuse the file rather than print an approximation.
invalid.name: extd-critical

invalid.description: An EXTD payload is four bytes, too short to carry ext_version and ext_type.
invalid.name: extd-truncated

invalid.description: An EXTD chunk sets reserved flag bit 0, which must be 0.
invalid.name: extd-reserved-flags

invalid.description: An EXTD ext_type is four non-ASCII bytes, so no reader can name the extension.
invalid.name: extd-type-nonascii

invalid.description: META's descriptor sets the encrypted bit while the file header does not, so the file carries no AUTH chunk and no key could open it.
invalid.name: sealed-without-auth

valid.description: Six layers over one sector covering the empty-layer form, binary REE, grayscale REE and split REE, in three LAYR chunks of two layers each with no dictionary, over a bottom range whose motion, wait and PWM values differ from the normal ones: the bottom layers take the bottom-prefixed values verbatim, the transition layer blends them, and light_pwm switches to the normal value at the first non-bottom layer instead of blending.
valid.name: binary-basic

valid.description: 64 layers with a trained ZDIC dictionary, in four LAYR chunks of sixteen layers each, every frame carrying the dictionary's id.
valid.name: dict-multi-block

valid.description: Four layers with two non-overlapping sectors, the second defined by META.sectors: layer 2 carries no data at all and is the empty layer, its single sector-0 entry holding a zero length, and two LROV chunks override one layer of one sector each - sector 1 of layer 0 and sector 0 of layer 1 - so the timing of a point is the timing of that point and not of its layer.
valid.name: multi-sector

valid.description: Ten layers over two sectors whose META.sectors entry for sector 1 carries bottom_layer_count 5 and no transition_layer_count, so sector 1 is blended over a bottom range of its own and inherits META's transition count; layer 4 is the layer where the two readings part, fully normal at 2500 ms for sector 0 and still a bottom layer at 30000 ms for sector 1, and their transition steps fall on layers 2 and 5 rather than together.
valid.name: sector-blend-ranges

valid.description: Password-mode AES-256-GCM: an Argon2id-wrapped session key, a sealed dictionary and metadata, and two LAYR chunks whose frames are sealed one by one under the directory index of the chunk that carries each.
valid.name: encrypted-password

valid.description: Machine-mode ChaCha20-Poly1305 with three recipient entries: a foreign machine, a decoy entry for our own fingerprint whose ephemeral key is the low-order point, and the real entry. A reader that unwraps the decoy without rejecting the all-zero shared secret recovers a different session key and cannot decrypt the file.
valid.name: encrypted-machine

valid.description: Both wrapping modes set in one AUTH chunk, with two sectors whose frames are sealed one by one, each under the directory index of the chunk that carries it.
valid.name: encrypted-both

valid.description: Password-mode AES-256-GCM with a sealed PROF chunk: profile identity, a material library, and a settings block reusing META's field names, including the experimental cure curve.
valid.name: print-profile

valid.description: Ten layers of one sector with seven LROV chunks: a single layer, a range of three layers written as one chunk per layer, a second range, and layer 4, which the first range covers too. An override set belongs to exactly one (layer, sector) - the entry that names the chunk is the only thing that places it - so nothing folds: layer 4 resolves to the values of its own set, which keeps the range's exposure and wait while taking the single-layer chunk's wait after the lift.
valid.name: layer-overrides

valid.description: Password-mode AES-256-GCM with two PREV chunks: a large preview in the clear and a sealed icon. Preview sealing is optional even when the file is encrypted, so both forms are valid in the same file.
valid.name: previews

valid.description: Password-mode AES-256-GCM with a sealed VOXL chunk: the scene bytes are copied in and must come back out unchanged, while LUMEN itself never parses them.
valid.name: embedded-scene

valid.description: Two non-critical EXTD chunks - one reserved ORA type code and one vendor extension - exercising the frame, the vendor id and critical flag bit, and the rule that readers skip extensions they do not implement.
valid.name: extensions
